newsitem.title: USA: Marks lead IMM currency futures to weak finish.
newsitem.headline: Marks lead IMM currency futures to weak finish.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended lower in marks, yen and Swiss francs after the dollar soared to a 71-month high against the mark in the U.S. afternoon.
September mark futures slumped to another in a long series of contract lows, bottoming at $0.5660, while dollar/mark rallied to fresh highs of 1.7775 after the close.
"Dollar/mark started the move," said an IMM floor analyst.
Swiss francs ended lower and near the day's low but remained above the September contract low of $0.6835 set in March.
One floor analyst said investors began buying sterling and selling marks Thursday, and the pressure on marks carried through to today.
The Bank of England Thursday raised official interest rates to 6.75 percent from 6.50 percent, the third increase in three months.

The prospect of higher British rates at a time when expectations for a soft single European currency are dragging on the mark helped propel sterling to an 81-month high today versus the German currency, the analysts said.
In IMM options trading, one U.S. investment house established a bearish position in the mark, buying 3,000 40-delta three-week July $0.5650 puts at 9.1 percent volatility, floor traders said.

September British pound futures rallied to a new six-month high at $1.6960 early before trimming gains. Traders projected the contract would encounter resistance at $1.7000 near term before mounting an assault on the contract high of $1.7020.
Yen futures slipped to the lowest level in over a week, but some analysts characterized the weakness as temporary and said they looked for the downtrend in dollar/yen to resume.

Mexican peso futures remained in a strong uptrend in active trading, with some analysts targeting an upside objective of $0.125800 next week in the September contract as the currency continues to draw strength from positive economic fundamentals and the July 6 election.

September Canadian dollar futures rose to a six-week high after the government released positive employment data, IMM traders said. The Canadian dollar was bolstered by news the country's jobless rate fell to 9.1 percent in June.

This morning's release of June U.S. producer price index data had little impact on currencies, floor traders said. Producer prices fell 0.1 percent from May, the sixth consecutive monthly drop. Core PPI excluding food and energy rose 0.1 percent, as forecast.

September yen futures ended down $0.000066 at $0.008856, marks down $0.0071 at $0.5663, Swiss francs down $0.0070 at $0.6881, sterling up $0.0040 at $1.6888, Canadian dollars up $0.0015 at $0.7327, Australian dollars down $0.0016 at $0.7413 and Mexican pesos up $0.000175 at $0.124225.
